summary: 403 on Console after successful Okta SSO — RBAC role-name normalization mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
Users are able to successfully authenticate via Okta SSO (SAML assertion verified and session created), but the Redwood Console returns a 403 Forbidden immediately after redirect. Affected users report they land on the Console landing page briefly and then see a 403 page.

Impact:
- Several admins and platform engineers are unable to access the Console for troubleshooting and deployments.
- No data plane impact; API keys and service accounts continue to operate.
- Incident blocking some operational work (P1).

Environment:
- Prod - us-east (single tenant auth pipeline)
- Okta org: redwood-prod.okta.com
- Console service version: v3.12.7 (frontend + auth-proxy)
steps_to_reproduce: Sign in to https://console.redwood.ai using Okta SSO (SAML) for a user expected to have 'platform/admin' role
Observe SAML assertion contains 'roles' attribute with value 'platform-admin' (legacy) or 'platform/admin' (new) depending on provisioning path
After successful SAML redirect, Console responds with 200 then immediately 403 on POST-auth role check
observed_behavior: SSO completes, session cookie set, but final authorization check fails with 403. Logs show auth-proxy receives roles claim 'platform-admin' while RBAC store expects 'platform/admin' key — normalization mismatch.
expected_behavior: User authenticated via SSO should be mapped to the Console RBAC role and allowed access consistent with group/role membership in Okta.
logs_and_traces: auth-proxy (2026-03-10T14:02:13Z): Received SAML assertion for user ravi.patel@redwood.ai; roles=['platform-admin']
investigation_notes: 03/10 14:05 - Confirmed affected users share common provisioning path: Okta SCIM rule path 'legacy-sso-to-platform'

03/10 15:12 - Recent change detected: infra/okta-provisioning introduced role-name normalization (replacing '-' with '/' for namespace compatibility) in commit 4f2d9a2; not all SCIM mappings were updated
03/10 16:45 - Reproduced locally by forging SAML assertion with roles='platform-admin' and observed RBAC lookup failure
03/11 09:20 - Cross-checked with INT-20671 (role propagation issues) — similar symptom but different root cause (that ticket was group propagation delay)

Hypothesis: A staggered rollout of role-name normalization changed how Okta SCIM writes role attributes for some users; auth-proxy expects normalized names but some SAML assertions still include legacy names, causing transient 403s
comments: Ravi Patel (2026-03-10): Added initial report and logs. Requesting priority triage as engineers are blocked.
Marta Nguyen (2026-03-10): Assigned for investigation. Will validate recent PRs to okta-provisioning and check SCIM logs.
SRE Team (2026-03-11): Confirmed auth-proxy accepts either form if RBAC service contains both aliases — currently RBAC store only contains normalized names.
Identity Team (2026-03-11): Found SCIM worker retries failing intermittently during a rollout window (see PR 742) — some users still have legacy role attribute.
Marta Nguyen (2026-03-12): Implemented temporary edge in auth-proxy to accept a mapped alias table (deployed to staging for validation)
Ravi Patel (2026-03-12): Staging validation looks good for replicated users; proceeding with canary deploy to prod auth-proxy
workaround: Temporary: Use direct console SSO bypass token (admin-only flow) or ask Identity to manually add normalized role entry in RBAC store for affected users. Not sustainable at scale.
next_steps: Deploy auth-proxy alias-mapping canary to 5% of auth traffic and monitor 403 rate
Identity to re-run SCIM reconciliation job for last 48h and surface remaining legacy-role users
If reconciliation is slow, create a one-time migration to bulk-write normalized role aliases into RBAC store to avoid 403s during rollout
resolution: In Progress - temporary alias mapping applied to auth-proxy canary; awaiting full SCIM reconciliation. Permanent fix pending coordinated rollout of role normalization in okta-provisioning and update of RBAC canonical names.
